takeaways: Rates are the story: the 10-year is above 5.1% and a December Fed hike is fully priced in, with Waller floating 50 bp. CBRE's average CRE loan rate hit 6.0% and alternative lenders now write 48% of closings, so lock in or hedge refi exposure now.

Multifamily distress is moving from operators to capital: big landlords are handing keys back to lenders (WSJ) and four Chicago investors account for about 30% of the city's multifamily foreclosures. Still, quality deals get funded, like Silverstein's $500M recap of 55 Broad with a $305M Wells Fargo loan.

Senior housing deals keep closing at sub-7% caps despite rising rates: LTC paid $62M for a 117-unit Florida AL/MC at a 6.5% cap, Discovery grew to 446 communities, and SRG, BWE and Lument placed $130M–$240M financings.

items.headline: Treasury 10-year holds above 5.1% as a December Fed hike is fully priced in
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield was about 5.12% on Nov. 16, with the 2-year at 4.84% and the 30-year at 5.46%. Futures put the odds of a 25 bp December hike from the 3.75–4.00% range at 91–100%, and Fed Governor Waller has said 50 bp 'should be considered.' For Lloyd Jones, that raises the cost of floating-rate debt and refis and makes rate caps more expensive going into 2027.

items.headline: Big landlords walk away from troubled apartment loans, leaving lenders with losses
items.summary: Deep-pocketed institutional owners are increasingly handing distressed multifamily properties back to lenders instead of putting in fresh equity, WSJ's Carol Ryan reports. Their strategic defaults are pushing losses onto lenders and could bring more distressed multifamily assets to market at discounts. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Four investors linked to 30% of Chicago multifamily foreclosures
items.summary: A Real Deal investigation ties Izzy Rotenberg, Chaim Bialostozky, Mark Nussbaum and Eliazer Tauber to about 30% of last year's Chicago multifamily foreclosures: 51 buildings and nearly 900 units, with Fannie and Freddie taking losses. The investigation describes related-party flips backed by inflated appraisals, including a 7-unit building bought for $245K in 2022 that got a $1.1M refi in 2024. Expect agencies to tighten appraisal and sponsor checks. (via The Promote)

items.headline: CBRE Q3 lending: alternative lenders take 48% of closings and average loan rate hits 6.0%
items.summary: The CBRE Lending Momentum Index fell to 0.7 from 1.0 in Q2. Commercial spreads averaged 197 bps and multifamily spreads 167 bps (7 bps tighter YoY). Alternative lenders' share of non-agency closings rose to 48% from 37%, while CMBS fell to 6%. The average mortgage rate rose to 6.0%, DSCR slipped to 1.32x and 82% of loans carried interest-only terms.

items.headline: Silverstein closes a $500M recap of the 55 Broad office-to-resi conversion
items.summary: RXR is leading a roughly $500M recap of the 571-unit 55 Broad conversion through its JV with the North Carolina Investment Authority. Wells Fargo is providing a $305M senior loan and Macquarie is also investing. Silverstein and Metro Loft bought the 410K sf building for $173M ($420/sf) in 2023, and market-rate rents now top $100/sf, evidence that well-executed conversions can still attract big capital. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Blackstone's new data center REIT debuts with a $5B AWS-tied portfolio
items.summary: Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust (BXDC) made its first deal a $5 billion acquisition of a stabilized data center portfolio tied to AWS. The purchase shows institutional capital still betting on AI-driven demand even as the AI trade gets more volatile. (via The Promote)

items.headline: LTC buys a 117-unit Florida AL/MC community for $62M at a 6.5% cap rate
items.summary: LTC Properties bought a 117-unit assisted living and memory care community in Florida, built in 2016, for $62M. Grace Management, a new operator relationship for LTC, will keep running it. LTC projects a 6.5% first-year cap rate and low- to mid-teens unlevered IRR, a useful pricing benchmark for newer AL/MC assets.

items.headline: Discovery takes over 26 SSMG communities and grows to 446 communities
items.summary: Discovery Senior Living took over management agreements for 26 communities (about 2,200 units) in eight Southern and Southeastern states from Senior Solutions Management Group. The mix is roughly two-thirds AL, 18% IL and 13% MC. Discovery now manages about 50,000 units across 446 communities in 40 states, a sign that third-party management keeps consolidating toward scaled operators.

items.headline: Blue-wave election throws Big Tech's data-center plans into question
items.summary: WSJ's Jinjoo Lee writes that November's Democratic wave has complicated data-center development, leaving some hyperscalers more exposed than others. Big Tech will need to spread its sites across more jurisdictions, which affects land, power and entitlement plays tied to AI demand. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: The month that rocked the AI trade and rewired Wall Street
items.summary: Volatility since the Nasdaq's Oct. 6 peak, through the election and Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia, has ended the 'no-brainer' era of broad AI bets. Investors now have to separate winners from losers. Nvidia reports earnings tonight, Nov. 17, after the close. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Senior living dealbook: Ventas adds three Charter-run communities; SRG lands $212.5M
items.summary: Ventas added three Southeast communities managed by Charter Senior Living, in Huntersville NC, Morehead City NC and Marietta GA, and Agemark bought River's Edge in Sacramento. In financings, Senior Resource Group arranged $212.5M for The Carrington at Lincolnwood, BWE placed a $240M recap of an Arrow-managed Midwest portfolio, and Lument made a $130M refi loan on Seattle's 243-unit Murano. Debt for quality senior housing is available even as base rates climb.

items.headline: Bevado raises a $10M seed for AI agents that automate resident communication
items.summary: RET Ventures led a $10M seed round in Bevado, with Pear VC participating. Bevado's AI agents coordinate maintenance repairs, update residents and collect post-service reviews. On the leasing side they call prospects before tours and follow up when interest fades, a relevant tool for both multifamily and senior living sales and maintenance teams.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO, expected at $1.33T or more, set to reward 300+ investors
items.summary: More than 300 investors, including VCs, big tech companies and sovereign-wealth funds, hold Anthropic stakes ahead of an IPO slated for this week, according to PitchBook. The listing is expected to value the company at $1.33 trillion or more. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Fifth Avenue rents jump 35%, reclaiming the world's top luxury retail crown
items.summary: Fifth Avenue rents rose an average of 35% over the past year, compared with 3% globally, according to Cushman & Wakefield. That puts it ahead of New Bond Street and Via Montenapoleone. Upper Fifth tenants pay about $2,700/sf, so any space over 371 sf costs more than $1M a year. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Berkshire nearly doubles its Lennar stake, doubling down on U.S. housing
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway nearly doubled its stake in home builder Lennar, adding to its bet on U.S. residential demand despite affordability strain and 5%+ long-term yields. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Struggling Long Island mall rebounds to 76% occupancy after an entertainment pivot
items.summary: Samanea New York in Westbury replaced fading retail with laser tag, trampolines, trapeze, escape rooms and axe-throwing. Occupancy rose to 76% from 22% in 2019, and Placer.ai data shows its foot traffic beating the indoor-mall sector. It's a template for repositioning distressed retail. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Activist Land & Buildings urges Invitation Homes to sell houses one at a time
items.summary: Jonathan Litt's Land & Buildings, which owns less than 1% of Invitation Homes, is pushing the SFR giant to sell homes individually to capture the gap between retail home prices and its public-market value. The Promote is skeptical, calling the firm a 'gnat' that is mainly skilled at getting press. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang gains steam as Nvidia reports earnings
items.summary: Elon Musk, Epic's Tim Sweeney and thousands of others have signed a 'Stand with Jensen' petition, and President Trump has said he 'would certainly not mind' a return. CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while the board searches for a replacement. It's a live case study in board governance, founder dependence and succession risk.

items.headline: Inside Nvidia's culture: public put-downs and a 'royal family' inner circle
items.summary: A WSJ investigation describes the demanding culture Jensen Huang built, marked by harsh public criticism and an elite inner circle. A senior employee warned the board that not reinstating Huang could cost 'irreplaceable talent.' It's a cautionary read on how leaders' personal styles become institutional risk. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: Whitehall: the rise and fall of Goldman's CRE machine and its alumni network
items.summary: The Promote looks back at Goldman's Whitehall Street funds under Dan Neidich. They raised the largest funds of the '90s and pre-GFC era and still returned about 75 cents on the dollar after the crash. Alumni now lead major platforms, including Neidich at Dune and Ralph Rosenberg at KKR real estate. (via The Promote)

items.headline: Job seekers in all 50 states describe a split labor market
items.summary: WSJ's Lindsay Ellis talked to more than 100 job seekers. Employed workers still get raises and corporate layoffs are down from last year, but laid-off white-collar workers and new graduates face their longest searches in years, which matters for recruiting and retention planning. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: More homeowners tap the $36 trillion in U.S. home equity
items.summary: Americans hold nearly $36 trillion in home equity and are increasingly pulling cash out to pay off credit cards and buy cars, ending years of post-2008 caution. Home equity is also a key funding source for seniors moving into senior living. (via WSJ 10-Point)

items.headline: A law partner who travels the globe for work without ever flying
items.summary: Scott Segal, 62, a D.C. international law partner, has reached Asia, Africa, Europe and Australia this year without boarding a plane, something he hasn't done since 1997. He travels by train, bus and cargo ship. (via WSJ 10-Point)
